mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-quarter increase in real GDP growth above 3% signals a robust expansionary demand environment, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations rise.
failure_condition: If real GDP growth exceeds 3% for 4 consecutive quarters but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of those instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month decline in the industrial production index below its 12-month moving average signals weakening manufacturing activity, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: If industrial production declines below its 12-month moving average for 6 months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of those instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs reduce corporate profitability.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate rises above 4.5% for 3 months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of those instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

failure_condition: If the unemployment rate rises above 7% for 6 months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of those instances, the hypothesis is falsified.
